request.deadline: 12-month delivery period from August 2026 to July 2027
deliverables: Frontend and backend maintenance and development
Independent audits of treasury fund use and oversight metrics
Introduction of Eternl Pro paid plans
On-chain reporting of paid Pro plans and publication of Pro earnings, repayment, and donation transaction hashes
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund 12 months of Eternl operations, maintenance, and improvements while it introduces paid Pro plans toward sustainability.

claims.claim: Eternl requests ₳2,350,000 at about $0.1787 per Ada to cover approximately $420,000 of annual operating costs for August 2026 through July 2027.
The proposal funds 6.0 FTE distributed across 10 contributors at $70,000 per FTE.
Eternl plans to introduce Pro plans priced at $96 per year for personal users and $360 per year for company users.
The proposer says about 4.2% of its install base, roughly 5,500 users, buying Pro would fully cover the annual $420,000 cost.
The proposer says Eternl has about 100,000 browser-extension installs and about 30,000 Android and iOS installs.
The proposer commits to convert up to $420,000 worth of Ada into stablecoins, place it in a public company wallet, and return any Ada above that amount to the treasury.
The audits allocation is for independent audits of treasury fund use and oversight metrics in February 2027 and August 2027, not technical security audits.

The proposer commits to semiannual treasury repayment using surplus remaining treasury stablecoins plus paid-plan income until $420,000 in Ada has been repaid, with possible additional donations capped at $210,000 worth of Ada.
The proposer states that 10-18% of Cardano mainnet transactions are conducted via Eternl.
The proposer states the main Eternl UI will not be open-source, while some Eternl libraries will be published through npm.

summary: The document requests ₳2,350,000 for a 12-month Eternl operating runway, describes a sustainability path through paid Pro plans, and includes commitments around public custody, audits, reporting, and partial or full treasury repayment, but many adoption and feasibility claims are asserted without in-document evidence.
